title: Cut This Animal's Oxygen for 18 Minutes. It Just Wakes Up Again

scenes.text: Cut off this animal's oxygen for 18 minutes. It shrugs.
In a chamber with no oxygen at all, it goes limp, slows its heart, and waits.
Its secret: it switches fuel. Brain cells stop burning glucose and start burning fructose, the sugar plants use.
Fructose makes energy without oxygen. In humans that pathway exists, but it's switched off.
At five percent oxygen, deadly for people and mice, it sat for five hours and looked fine.
Why? Hundreds of them share airless tunnels where carbon dioxide hits ten percent. Oxygen back, it wakes in seconds.

description:
Cut off this animal's oxygen for 18 minutes and it simply wakes up again when the air comes back.
The naked mole rat survives total oxygen deprivation by switching its brain from glucose to fructose, a sugar it can burn without oxygen, a pathway that exists in humans but is switched off. At 5 percent oxygen, a level lethal to people and mice, it sat for five hours and looked fine. It evolved this in crowded, poorly ventilated burrows where carbon dioxide can reach 10 percent. Published in Science in 2017.
Which animal superpower would you most want?
subject: naked mole rat
first_comment: Naked mole rats also live past 30, far longer than any other rodent of their size. What else should we dig into about them?
